extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark collection takes three stages: 1) selecting subjects based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted; 2) recruiting over 50 university students as annotators to collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary; 3) performing data quality control including duplicate removal, format checking, and difficulty categorization.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions collected from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Data cleaning steps: lexical overlap and source URL similarity to identify duplicates, format and typo checking, and categorization into difficulty levels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Approximately 10% of problems classified as very easy were excluded from the benchmark. The dataset is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators (university students) collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. They adhered to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A live-updating leaderboard is available at: https://mmmu-benchmark.github.io/#leaderboard
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is designed to monitor progress towards Expert AGI, which could lead to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI as per the definition because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation. The benchmark is designed to evaluate multimodal models on expert-level tasks.
